name: Treadmill Sprint Intervals
description: Treadmill sprint intervals alternate short bursts of maximal or near-maximal running speed with active recovery periods at a slow jog or walk. The repeated acceleration and deceleration demands high power output from the quadriceps, hamstrings, and gluteus maximus while imposing strong cardiovascular stress. Sprint intervals are time-efficient for improving both aerobic capacity and anaerobic power, and produce a significant post-exercise calorie burn through excess post-exercise oxygen consumption (EPOC).

execution.starting_position: Begin with a 5-minute warm-up walk at 3–4 mph, gradually increasing to a light jog. Stand on the treadmill with feet straddling the belt, then step on when the belt reaches sprint speed — or accelerate from the jog speed.
execution.setup_instructions: Set the sprint speed before the interval begins. For safety on a treadmill, pre-set the target sprint speed, then straddle the belt and step on when it reaches that speed, rather than accelerating mid-stride. Alternatively, build up from a jog.
steps: Step 1: Warm up for 5 minutes with a walk progressing to an easy jog.
Step 2: Increase belt speed to sprint pace (8–12 mph / 13–19 km/h depending on fitness). Sprint for 20–30 seconds.
Step 3: Reduce speed immediately to walk or slow jog (3–4 mph). Recover for 60–90 seconds.
Step 4: Repeat the sprint-recovery cycle 6–10 times.
Step 5: Cool down with a 5-minute walk, gradually reducing speed.
execution.breathing_instructions: During sprints, breathe as forcefully as needed — do not try to control breathing rhythm. During recovery, focus on deep, controlled exhalations to lower heart rate faster.
common_mistakes: Holding the handrails during the sprint, which completely changes the biomechanics and reduces the training stimulus
Setting the sprint speed too high before building a base, increasing fall risk
Skipping the warm-up, which raises injury risk for hamstrings and hip flexors
safety_considerations: Never jump onto a treadmill moving at sprint speed from a standing start — accelerate progressively
Know how to emergency-stop the machine before beginning sprints
Clip the safety key to your clothing
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Full hip extension behind the body during the push-off phase is the goal. Knee drive upward should bring the thigh roughly parallel to the ground during the swing phase.
execution.tempo_recommendations: Classic protocol: 20–30 seconds sprint / 90 seconds recovery × 8 rounds. Tabata variation: 20 seconds sprint / 10 seconds walk × 8 rounds.
coaching_cues: Drive the elbows back forcefully — arm drive powers the legs
Stay on the balls of the feet, not the heels
Push the belt away behind you — attack each stride
